set.body:
WHY: retrieval workloads send many small query graphs against a prepared source set. WLQueryTrace/WLQueryAlignment exist but: CSR.row allocates a dense length-F vector per query, the output is a dense QxT matrix, SampleIndex.indexOf is linear, and there is no incremental single-query path or sparse row access. Correctness of the overlay (no contamination of the source dictionary) is asserted in code comments, not laws.

SCOPE: expose sparse per-row access on FeatureMatrix (no dense allocation); an incremental query API (prepare once; query(sample) -> sparse row + sparse cross vector); index lookups O(1) or O(log n); benchmarks.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (law G3 from storymodel4s ADR 0001)
1. Immutability: the prepared source state (dictionary, features, gram) is unchanged after any number of queries (structural equality + fingerprint equality).
2. No contamination: query-only colours never appear in the source dictionary; their mass appears only in novelSquaredNorm.
3. Exactness: for random small oracles, cross values from the overlay == values from recompiling source+query together (within 1e-12), and single-query results == batch results.
4. Scaling: time per query is O(size of query graph + nnz of its row + matched training nnz), measured: 10k queries of ~20 vertices against 5k prepared graphs completes with peak allocation independent of F (no length-F dense temporaries); benchmark report committed under benchmarks/.
5. Sparse row access: FeatureMatrix.sparseRow(i) returns (indices, values) without materializing a dense vector.

PROPOSED TESTS
- OverlayImmutabilitySuite: hash prepared state before/after 1000 queries.
- OverlayNoContaminationSuite: property — dictionary size and contents invariant; novel norm > 0 iff query has a colour absent from source.
- OverlayExactnessSuite: property — recompile oracle vs overlay; single vs batch.
- SparseRowSuite: sparseRow(i) equals dense row's nonzeros; no allocation of length F (assert via a counting allocator hook or by bounding memory in a JVM microbenchmark).
- QueryBench (JMH or the existing benchmark worker): documented numbers with the machine fingerprint.
